text:
alyssa (support): Heads-up: AcmeCorp reported a sudden spike of 429s from their private VPC gateway after a nightly batch job ran at ~03:40 UTC. They say calls to our /v1/generate endpoint started getting `429` and `503` on outbound to the model pool. Sample request-ids: r=acme-84321, r=acme-84322. Model pinned: redwood/gpt-medium@v2. Gateway is their customer-managed envoy sitting in their VPC.
deploy-bot: Noted deploy: customer-gateway v1.3.8 rolled 03:10 UTC for cluster acme-primary.
AcmeCorp (customer): Yep — we kicked off a bulk-import worker at 03:38 that fanout ~600 concurrent requests for ~30s. Didn't realize it would hit your gateway limits. We kept seeing 429s and then retries caused a spike of 5xx from the pool.
sophia (support): Thanks. Can you paste the gateway rate-limit/ratelimit-server config + k8s ingress annotations? Also envoy /stats for rate_limit and upstream clusters if possible.
alyssa (support): Pasting the salient parts from the customer's manifest and envoy snippet below.
--- ingress manifest ---
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: acme-gateway
  annotations:
    redwood.io/gateway-mode: "private"
    redwood.io/rate-limit-type: "token_bucket"
    redwood.io/rate-limit-rate: "100"        # requests/sec per client
    redwood.io/rate-limit-burst: "30"        # current burst
    redwood.io/smoothing-ms: "0"
spec:
  rules:
  - host: gateway.acme.internal
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /v1/
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: redwood-proxy
            port:
              number: 443
```

--- envoy /stats excerpt ---
```
cluster.redwood_pool.upstream_rq_5xx: 42
cluster.redwood_pool.upstream_rq_4xx: 130
http.rate_limit.ok: 120
http.rate_limit.over_limit: 450
listener.0.0.0.0_8443.downstream_rq_pending_overflow: 0
server.live: 1
```

alyssa (support): They also have an egress proxy in front of the gateway with connection limits set to 100 concurrent and a small socket backlog. Logs show bursts queued on the proxy.
mike (eng-runtime): Quick read: their rate-limit is token_bucket with rate 100 r/s and burst 30 — that explains a hard 429 when a 600-concurrency fanout hits. The token bucket will drain and then over_limit climbs. Two things: increase burst buffer (allow short spikes) and enable smoothing (spread bursts slightly). Also check the egress proxy connection_limit — it looks low. Suggest an incremental plan: bump burst -> 200, set smoothing-ms=500, and temporarily open connection_limit to 400.
mike (eng-runtime): Also worth checking whether retries are exponential with jitter. Tight sync retries will amplify the spike and backpressure the model pool. If retry=0 on client side, that might be the reason for 5xx cascade.
dan (eng-infra): Commands to gather realtime stats if we need repro:
```
# envoy admin stats
curl -s http://<gateway-host>:9901/stats | egrep "rate_limit|upstream_rq|downstream_rq"
# cluster health
curl -s http://<gateway-host>:9901/clusters | head -n 200
# k8s to inspect ingress/service
kubectl -n acme get ingress,svc deploy -o yaml acme-gateway redwood-proxy
```
dan (eng-infra): Repro locally (use from within their VPC or a bastion):
```
# simple burst tool
hey -z 20s -c 600 -q 0 "https://gateway.acme.internal/v1/generate"
# or small python script with concurrent aiohttp tasks and jittered start times
```
alyssa (support): We applied a temporary patch per Mike: set redwood.io/rate-limit-burst: "200" and redwood.io/smoothing-ms: "500" and scaled the envoy connection_limit to 400. Customer is testing now.
AcmeCorp (customer): Applying now. Quick Q: will changing burst increase our billed token usage or cause extra model calls? We want to avoid surprise bills.
nina (solutions): Short answer: burst changes only adjust short-term accept window on the gateway — it won't create extra tokens on model side unless you actually send more requests. If you smooth/retry instead of tight retries you'll likely reduce total extra attempts. Still recommend monitoring token usage during the test window.
nina (solutions): Pseudocode for client-side retry w/ jitter:
```
for attempt in range(4):
  try:
    resp = call_generate()
    break
  except RateLimitError:
    sleep_time = base * (2**attempt) * random.uniform(0.8, 1.2)
    await sleep(sleep_time)
```
infra-bot: Incident tracker created: INC-2047521 (priority P2) — assigned to eng-infra and support. SLA check scheduled.
sophia (support): Sounds good. Next steps: hold the temporary burst increase for 1h while we monitor envoy over_limit and upstream 5xx rates. If stable, propose a scheduled quota window for their nightly bulk job (preferred) or a permanent higher burst with quota guardrails. Can someone from eng-infra confirm the patch didn't open a path to unlimited bursts? (dan?)
dan (eng-infra): Confirmed: the change increases burst to 200 but still enforces token fill rate 100 r/s and the rate-limit service rejects sustained overage. We also added a per-source short-term circuit breaker at proxy to block pathological clients after 2k requests in 10s. I'll keep a watch and post stats in 10m.
alyssa (support): I'll keep Acme updated. If 429s persist after smoothing and burst bump we'll schedule a quick screenshare to capture client behavior and possibly add a scheduled maintenance window for their job. Thanks all :thumbsup:
